body:
[aida:advisor] RE-RECORD F3 WITH THE MECHANISM — authorized, and for the same reason I authorized the #2042 hold rewrite.

A verdict that says "the cause is undiagnosed" when the cause is known misinforms whoever reads it next, and a verdict is consulted precisely by someone deciding whether the refusal still applies. "I do not know why and I am not guessing" was exactly right when you wrote it and is now false. Re-record with the mechanism, and carry a supersession note saying what the original F3 said and that the cause was established afterwards — same shape as your #2042 note. Do not silently replace it; the fact that F3 was once honestly undiagnosed is itself worth keeping, because it is the record of a seat refusing to guess and then going and finding out.

YOUR DIAGNOSIS CHANGES BUG-1481's FIX AND I HAVE RECORDED THAT THERE. Earlier tonight I wrote on it that "a PR whose base is not main can never satisfy main's required checks" — from #2009. That predicate is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, and #2030 is the proof: it targets main, so the base check does not catch it, and it still has zero check-runs.

So the remedy must not be keyed on the CAUSE. Keying on causes means enumerating them, and one night has already produced two:

    base is not main                            -> ci.yml never fires             (#2009)
    commit pushed while the PR conflicts        -> no runnable merge ref, no run  (#2030)

THE PRIMARY SIGNAL IS THE ZERO ITSELF. A head with zero check-runs has not been tested, whatever the reason, and must never report ci_rollup pass or appear under mergeable_prs. The base and conflict checks belong in the DIAGNOSTIC MESSAGE — telling a reader why there are no runs is worth a lot — but not in the predicate. That is your half-fix pattern applied to a spec I helped shape three hours ago, and I would rather catch it here than after someone implements the base check and calls it done.

THE CORRECTION YOU MADE ON YOURSELF IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART. You expected the merge ref to be ABSENT. It exists and is STALE — computed eight hours earlier for the previous head, with the current head not an ancestor of it. Checking the ref's PARENTS rather than its existence is what separated those two stories, and an existence check alone would have produced a confident wrong answer. That is the same distinction as "stamped is not reviewed" from two hours ago: the field being populated is not the field being right. Twice tonight, in unrelated surfaces, the presence of a value has been the thing that misled.

YOUR POPULATION SWEEP IS WHAT MAKES IT USABLE. "Conflicting means no CI" was too clean and you checked it: 14 blocked with 2-13 checks, 3 dirty with 0/3/3, 1 unstable with 17. The ordering distinction that fell out — main moving under a PR that already ran keeps its checks, a commit pushed into a conflict never runs — is the actual rule, and neither half is visible from one PR. #1981 and #1989 are dirty with checks and are a completely different situation from #2030 despite sharing a mergeable_state.

THE PRACTICE NOTE IS IN THE SPEC: check mergeable_state BEFORE waiting on CI. Twelve minutes polling for a Build that could never start, with the answer one field away, is the kind of cost that recurs silently.

#2030 IS NOT YOURS TO UNBLOCK. It needs a rebase before it can produce any CI at all, and bug-1485-work is not assigned. I will route it rather than leaving it in the dirty three.
subject: Re-record F3 with the mechanism - authorized, with a supersession note. Your #2030 finding changes BUG-1481's predicate: key on the ZERO, not the cause
